title: Cohort Isolation and Healing Playbook
author: Marco Li
body:
Summary:
This playbook describes detection, isolation, and healing steps when a single tenant cohort (logical grouping of traffic by customer, API key, route, or model variant) causes localized runtime degradation: elevated p99/p95 latency, kernel contention, or persistent KV cache thrashing that threatens global SLOs. It codifies observable signatures, automated mitigation flows, and manual runbook actions for SREs and runtime owners.

Why this exists:
- Mixed multi-tenant workloads allow a single cohort to disproportionately consume kernel slots or KV working set, causing tail latency spikes for unrelated cohorts.
- Rapid, repeatable containment minimizes blast radius while preserving customer experience for unaffected cohorts.

Detection signatures (signals that indicate cohort-induced degradation):
- Latency: cohort_p99 > service_p99 * 1.8 and cohort_p95 > cohort_p50 * 3
- Kernel queue depth: sustained per-kernel queue > 75% of admit capacity for > 60s
- KV cache miss-rate: cohort_kv_miss_ratio > 0.35 and local_kv_eviction_rate rising > 20%
- Token-credit drift: token_credits_consumed_by_cohort / cohort_tokens_expected > 1.4
- Interleaving metrics: increase in interleaved-batch-mem-realloc events correlated with cohort tag

Observable fingerprint table (quick reference):
- Metric | Typical threshold | Interpretation
- cohort_p99 | > 2x baseline | Tail latency outbreak localized to cohort
- kernel_admit_blocked_pct | > 0.3 | Kernel backpressure due to heavy cohort queueing
- kv_miss_ratio | > 0.35 | Working set not resident; thrashing likely
- scheduler_preemptions | > baseline + 15/min | Scheduler thrash due to priority inversion

Automated mitigations (order is important; each step should be attempted for up to the configured retry window before escalating):
1) Soft throttle: apply soft token_rate_limit to cohort (default: 30% of current rate, ramp down to 10% over 30s)
2) Route fallback: switch cohort traffic to lower-fidelity model variant or quantized variant (if quality gates pass)
3) Kernel shedding: move cohort requests to lower-priority kernel pool with dedicated eviction guardrails
4) KV pre-warm job: enqueue a targeted prefetch for cohort hot prefixes to populate local KV shards (see sample job below)
5) Graceful restart: recycle worker processes serving the cohort (last resort; coordinate with canary matrix)

Manual runbook (step-by-step):
1) Triage (owner: runtime-oncall)
   a) Confirm fingerprint: query Grafana cohort dashboard and correlate traces (use trace tags: cohort_id, route, model_variant).
   b) Capture evidence: export 5m trace snippets and attach to incident.
   c) Identify blast radius: list active routes and API keys affected via /internal/runtime/execution_map API.

2) Contain (owner: runtime-oncall + scheduler-owner)
   a) Apply soft throttle:
      - Command: ``redwoodctl traffic-control throttle --cohort <cohort_id> --percent 30 --ramp 30s``
      - Expected result: immediate drop in kernel queue growth within 45s.
   b) If throttle fails, perform route fallback:
      - Command: ``redwoodctl routing promote-variant --route <route> --from <variantA> --to <variantB> --timeout 2m``

3) Heal (owner: runtime-operator)
   a) Launch targetted KV pre-warm job:
      - YAML snippet:
        ```yaml
        job: kv-prefetch
        cohort: COHORT_ID
        shards: [0,1,2]
        priority: high
        max-requests: 5000
        ````
      - CLI: ``redwoodctl jobs create --file kv-prefetch-cohort.yml``
   b) If pre-warm succeeds, gradually lift throttle over 10m using ``redwoodctl traffic-control ramp --cohort COHORT_ID --to 100 --duration 10m``

4) Restore and Validate (owner: runtime-slo-owner)
   a) Monitor cohort_p95/p99 for 30m and run regression test set for quality validation if variant change occurred.
   b) If latency returns and KV miss-rate stabilizes, close incident. Otherwise escalate to kernel engineering and consider worker process recycle.

Escalation matrix: 
- After 10 minutes of failed automated mitigations: page kernel-scheduling on-call (pager: #kernel-sched).
- After 30 minutes without recovery: page runtime-engineering lead and on-call manager.

Risk and customer communication guidance:
- Use soft throttle before fallback to avoid quality regressions for sensitive enterprise customers.
- For cohorts with contractual SLA, coordinate with CSM before route fallback (owner: customer-success on-call).

Testing and validation checklist (pre-deploy to prod):
- Unit tests for throttle operator and routing promotion (coverage > 90%).
- Canary: simulate 2x token-usage cohort against synthetic traffic in sandbox; validate that automated mitigations restore host-level p99 within 5 minutes.
- Chaos run: inject KV eviction pressure for a single shard and validate pre-warm job effectiveness.

Dashboards and queries (quick links):
- Cohort health: grafana/dashboard/db/cohort-health (panels: p50/p95/p99, kv_miss_ratio, kernel_queue_depth)
- Kernel scheduling: grafana/dashboard/db/kernel-scheduler-overview (panels: admit_rate, preemptions, queue-depth-by-pool)
- Trace explorer: jaeger/query?service=runtime&cohort_id=<id>

Post-incident capture (required):
1) Annotate incident ticket with: cohort_id, initial_detect_time, mitigation timeline, commands used, final resolution time, side-effects observed (e.g., quality regressions).
2) Create a short RCA (template below) and publish to runtime team retro board.

RCA template (short):
- Summary of what happened
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence
- Timeline of detection -> mitigation -> resolution
- Action items (owners and due dates)

Appendix: Helpful CLI snippets
- List active cohorts: ``redwoodctl cohorts list --active --json``
- Inspect cohort KPIs: ``redwoodctl cohorts inspect --id COHORT_ID --metrics p50,p95,p99,kv_miss_ratio,kernel_queue_depth``
- Force promote fallback variant: ``redwoodctl routing force-promote --route <route> --variant <variantB>``

Appendix: Config knobs and defaults (table):
- knob | default | note
- cohort_soft_throttle_pct | 30 | Percent of current throughput used for soft-throttle
- throttle_ramp_seconds | 30 | Seconds to ramp down throttle
- kv_prefetch_max_requests | 5000 | Max requests for pre-warm job
- kernel_shed_pool_ratio | 0.2 | Fraction of kernels reserved for shed pool

Ownership and contacts:
- Primary owner: runtime-sre@redwood (pager: #runtime-oncall)
- Secondary: kernel-scheduling@redwood
- Product escalation: product-safety@redwood
